mission.title: Fishy
mission.description: Destroy the overridden programs in the slums and follow the trail of the biological interface program.

npc.say: They have their uses--keeping Agents away, for instance--but they are crude, and limited. They are weapons only, and not the tool I need for my work.

phase.briefing: Operative, available data indicates that the biological interface program has moved from the Merovingian's Hel Club into Richland. Danielle Wright has been tenacious in her pursuit of the program, and, as was to be expected, override use has now spiked in the slums. The overridden programs cannot be allowed to remain active.

enter.say: There be overrides... Hey, I'm reading what look like redpill signals in there, too.

done.say: Huh. I'll see if we can access transfer logs on that thing.

phase.briefing: We anticipate continued encounters with hostile forces. Zion as well as Merovingian operatives have been gathering in the central Richland area.

enter.say: Okay, so, I got a transfer history showing that the computer we found connected to a system in an apartment there.
There's a signal in there, but not a big one; and I don't see any overrides.

done.say:
They want us to find...a cat?
I'm really not sure if we should even tell Gray about this...

phase.briefing: If we can focus on the task at hand, {player}.

enter.say:
Got some signals in there. Based on the hacks I'm picking up...I'd say they're redpills.
They say that at the meeting in One Zero, Wright was bragging about entering the Matrix as a "complete consciousness," or some kind of crazy thing. Sounds like a load of metaphysical baloney if you ask me.

done.say: Damn! Just when you almost think a Zionite's about to be useful for once...

phase.briefing: Zionite and Merovingian forces are understood to be attempting to acquire the interface program. Their operatives claim to have received fragmentary messages from the program; the nonsensical nature of these reports suggests that they are intended to manipulate susceptible humans.

enter.say:
Well, Gray did tell Wright in One Zero that the Oracle made the program to help keep tabs on unplugged humans. Seems to be causing an awful lot of ruckus just for that. Could explain why Wright would want it, though.
Uh-oh, it looks like we've hit some of those overrides we've been hearing about. Wonder what those would do to the interface program...?

talk.say: The program has moved on, if that's what you're wondering. Its movements appear to be getting less erratic. In the right hands, it could be a truly elegant control mechanism--not like these Oligarch routines.

So the program got away again. Well, at least she didn't get her wiry mitts on it.
Wonder what she meant by "control mechanism," though. Gray said the Oracle made it to control awakened humans. Could that be Wright's plan?

mission.finish:
Wright appears to be under some misapprehension about the program, which could possibly be turned to our advantage. It is true, however, that it would be dangerous for the simulation if it fell under her control. Our sensors, for instance, cannot detect the program directly; this complicates the task of keeping it from her.
Oh... One other thing, {player}: you may be glad to hear that "Ms. Pickles" was found in an alley in Mara, and returned safely to her owner.
